thought_title: One Prayer, One Altar, One Christ

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ὥσπερ οὖν ὁ κύριος ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς οὐδὲν ἐποίησεν, ἡνωμένος ὤν, οὔτε δἰ ἑαυτοῦ οὔτε διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων: οὕτως μηδὲ ὑμεῖς ἄνευ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων μηδὲν πράσσετε: μηδὲ πειράσητε εὔλογόν τι φαίνεσθαι ἰδίᾳ ὑμῖν, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ μία προσευχή, μία δέησις, εἷς νοῦς, μία ἐλπὶς ἐν ἀγάπῃ, ἐν τῇ χαρᾷ τῇ ἀμώμῳ, ὅ ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, οὖ ἄμεινον οὐδέν ἐστιν. [2] πάντες ὡς εἰς ἕνα ναὸν συντρέχετε θεοῦ, ὡς ἐπὶ ἓν θυσιαστήριον, ἐπὶ ἕνα Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, τὸν ἀφ̓ ἑνὸς πατρὸς προελθόντα καὶ εἰς ἕνα ὄντα καὶ χωρήσαντα.
pass_a_gloss: So just as the Lord did nothing without the Father, being united with him, neither by himself nor through the apostles, so you too do nothing without the bishop and the presbyters. And do not try to make anything appear reasonable to you privately; but, gathered together in one place, let there be one prayer, one petition, one mind, one hope, in love, in blameless joy, which is Jesus Christ, than whom nothing is better. All of you, run together as to one temple of God, as to one altar, to one Jesus Christ, who came forth from one Father, and is with the One, and returned to him.
pass_b_english: The Lord was one with the Father and did nothing without him (John 5:19): nothing on his own, nothing through the apostles. In the same way, you must do nothing without the bishop and the presbyters. Do not try to make some private course look reasonable to yourselves. Come together in one place: one prayer, one plea, one mind, one hope, in love, in spotless joy. That joy is Jesus Christ, and nothing is better than he.
Run together, all of you, as to one temple of God, as to one altar, to one Jesus Christ. He came forth from one Father; he is with that One; and to that One he has returned.

choices.term: ἐν τῇ χαρᾷ τῇ ἀμώμῳ, ὅ ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός
choices.english: in spotless joy. That joy is Jesus Christ
choices.why: The relative clause names the joy as Jesus Christ; we keep that identity rather than a new sentence 'There is one Jesus Christ'.
rejected: There is one Jesus Christ, than whom nothing is more excellent

choices.english: one prayer, one plea, one mind, one hope
choices.why: His liturgical 'one' cadence kept word for word.
rejected: a single prayer and a shared mind

choices.english: he is with that One; and to that One he has returned
choices.why: εἰς with both participles: being in/with the One and having gone back to him.
rejected: is with and has gone to one

choices.english: make some private course look reasonable to yourselves
choices.why: ἰδίᾳ sets private judgment against the common assembly.
rejected: anything appear reasonable and proper to yourselves apart

anf_compare.notes: ANF ends the sentence after 'joy undefiled' and starts 'There is one Jesus Christ'; the Greek ὅ ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός says the blameless joy is Jesus Christ. Otherwise same sense.

bible_refs.note: Son does nothing of himself (οὐ ... ποιεῖν ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ οὐδέν); also compare John 8:28.

notes: 'Being united with him' may echo John 10:30; 'in one place' (ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό) may echo Acts 2:1, 44. Not cited inline.
The 'one ... one' list may recall Ephesians 4:4-6; pattern only, not cited inline.
Source shows 'δἰ' for δι’ and 'ἀφ̓' with a variant breathing mark; reproduced as supplied.

review.notes: P1 checked clause by clause. ‘Ὥσπερ οὖν ὁ κύριος ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς οὐδὲν ἐποίησεν, ἡνωμένος ὤν, οὔτε δἰ ἑαυτοῦ οὔτε διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων’ is kept in A as ‘did nothing without the Father, being united with him, neither by himself nor through the apostles’ and in B as ‘did nothing without him … nothing on his own, nothing through the apostles.’ Imperatives πράσσετε / πειράσητε / συντρέχετε stay commands; ‘μηδὲ … ἰδίᾳ ὑμῖν’ stays a ban on private reasonableness. ‘μία προσευχή, μία δέησις, εἷς νοῦς, μία ἐλπὶς’ and ‘ὅ ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, οὖ ἄμεινον οὐδέν ἐστιν’ match ‘one prayer… one hope’ and ‘which is Jesus Christ, than whom nothing is better.’ ‘προελθόντα καὶ εἰς ἕνα ὄντα καὶ χωρήσαντα’ matches ‘came forth from one Father, and is with the One, and returned.’ (John 5:19) follows the supplied wording note, not a shifted verse. Title names the unity thought.

Pass A omits the explicit citation to John 5:19 required by the source's bible_refs. The Greek contains no inline citation, but the apparatus identifies John 5:19 as the scriptural basis for 'Ὥσπερ οὖν ὁ κύριος ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς οὐδὲν ἐποίησεν, ἡνωμένος ὤν, οὔτε δἰ ἑαυτοῦ οὔτε διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων'. Pass A renders this as 'So just as the Lord did nothing without the Father, being united with him, neither by himself nor through the apostles' without adding '(John 5:19)' or equivalent. Per rules: added identifications are REQUIRED; fail only a wrong verse, never the practice. Since the apparatus specifies John 5:19 and Pass A omits it, this is a missing citation. Also, Pass A's clause 'And do not try to make anything appear reasonable to you privately; but, gathered together in one place...' adds 'but, gathered together in one place' which is not in the Greek. The Greek has 'μηδὲ πειράσητε εὔλογόν τι φαίνεσθαι ἰδίᾳ ὑμῖν, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ μία προσευχή...' — the 'ἀλλ’' introduces the positive alternative directly after the prohibition, but Pass A inserts 'but, gathered together in one place' as a separate clause, altering the structure. The Greek does not say 'gathered together in one place' until paragraph 2; here it is an anticipatory addition not in the text.
reasons: Pass A omits required scriptural citation John 5:19 for the Lord's action in relation to the Father, despite apparatus identification.

Pass A adds 'but, gathered together in one place' after 'do not try to make anything appear reasonable to you privately', which is not in the Greek clause and shifts the meaning by inserting an anticipatory element from paragraph 2.
